# 45 Recto

The assemblies of perfected beings praise you with abundant hymns. (21) The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, the Sadhyas, the Vishvedevas, the two Ashvins, the Maruts, and the Ushmapas, as well as the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas, all look upon you with wonder. (22) O mighty-armed one, seeing your great form with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs, and feet, many bellies, and many terrible tusks, the worlds are terrified, and so am I. (23) Seeing you touching the sky, shining, many-colored, with gaping mouths and flaming, enormous eyes, my inner soul is terrified, O Vishnu, and I find neither steadfastness nor peace. (24) Seeing your mouths, terrible with tusks, like the fires of time,

<column-break/>

# 45 Verso

I lose my sense of direction and find no shelter. Be gracious, O Lord of gods, O Dwelling-place of the universe. (25) All these sons of Dhritarashtra, <unclear>with the hosts of kings</unclear>, together with Bhishma, Drona, the son of the charioteer <note>a reference to Karna</note>, as well as our own warrior chiefs, (26) are rushing into your mouths, which are terrible with tusks and frightening. Some are seen stuck between your teeth, their heads crushed. (27) Just as the many currents of rivers rush toward the ocean alone, so do these heroes of the human world enter your flaming mouths. (28) Just as moths rush into a blazing fire <unclear>to their destruction</unclear>.

<note>A circular hole is situated in the center of the palm leaf to accommodate a binding cord.</note>

<summary>This passage describes Arjuna's vision of the cosmic form of Krishna, expressing terror at the destructive power displayed before the great battle.</summary>
<keywords>Bhagavad Gita, Krishna, Arjuna, Cosmic Form, Vishvarupa, divine terror, destruction</keywords>
